definition_title: pp. 4, 7–8, 12, 15, 18 — codes of Tanner graphs, minimum distance (∞ for {0}), CSS distance and dimension, the hypergraph product H_X, H_Z, product codes
natural_language_statement:
This file fixes the objects of Tillich and Zémor's hypergraph-product construction. Everything is linear algebra over the binary field $\mathbb F_2$.

1. **Codes of Tanner graphs.** A Tanner graph $\mathcal T(V,C,E)$ is the bipartite graph of a parity-check matrix $H=(h_{cv})$ with rows indexed by the check nodes $C$ and columns by the variable nodes $V$; there is an edge $c\sim v$ iff $h_{cv}=1$. Its code is $\mathcal C=\ker H=\{x\in\mathbb F_2^V : Hx=0\}$. The **transpose** Tanner graph is that of $H^{T}$, and its code $\mathcal C^{T}=\ker H^{T}\subseteq\mathbb F_2^{C}$ depends on $H$, not only on $\mathcal C$.
2. **Minimum distance.** For a linear code $D\subseteq\mathbb F_2^\iota$, $d(D)=\min\{|x| : x\in D,\ x\neq 0\}$, where $|x|$ is the Hamming weight; by the convention of p. 15, $d(\{0\})=\infty$.
3. **CSS distance and dimension** (eqs (1)–(2)). For linear codes $A=\mathcal C_X$ and $B=\mathcal C_Z$ of the same length,
$$d_X=\min\{|x| : x\in A\setminus B^{\perp}\},\qquad k_Q=\dim\big(A/(B^{\perp}\cap A)\big),$$
with $\min\emptyset=\infty$; $d_Z$ is $d_X$ with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged. Here $B^\perp$ is the dual code for the standard dot product.
4. **The quantum code $\mathcal Q(\mathcal G_1\times\mathcal G_2)$** (Definition 3, in the matrix form of p. 18). For $H_1\in\mathbb F_2^{C_1\times V_1}$ and $H_2\in\mathbb F_2^{C_2\times V_2}$ the qubits are indexed by $(V_1\times V_2)\sqcup(C_1\times C_2)$ and
$$H_X=\big(H_1\otimes I_{V_2}\ \big|\ I_{C_1}\otimes H_2^{T}\big),\qquad H_Z=\big(I_{V_1}\otimes H_2\ \big|\ H_1^{T}\otimes I_{C_2}\big),$$
with rows indexed by $C_1\times V_2$ and $V_1\times C_2$ respectively. Row $(c_1,v_2)$ of $H_X$ is the set of variables $(v_1,v_2)$ with $v_1\sim c_1$ together with the variables $(c_1,c_2)$ with $c_2\sim v_2$, which is the neighbourhood of the check $(c_1,v_2)$ in the product graph. Then $\mathcal C_X=\ker H_X$, $\mathcal C_Z=\ker H_Z$, $d_Q=\min(d_X,d_Z)$ and $k_Q=\dim(\mathcal C_X/\mathcal C_Z^{\perp})$.
5. **The hypergraph product $\mathcal G_1\otimes\mathcal G_2$** (Definition 7) is the Tanner graph with variable nodes $V_1\times V_2$, check nodes $(C_1\times V_2)\sqcup(V_1\times C_2)$, and parity-check matrix $\binom{H_1\otimes I_{V_2}}{I_{V_1}\otimes H_2}$.
6. **The product code** (Definition 8). For $D_1\subseteq\mathbb F_2^{\iota_1}$ and $D_2\subseteq\mathbb F_2^{\iota_2}$, $D_1\otimes D_2$ is the set of $\iota_1\times\iota_2$ binary matrices all of whose columns lie in $D_1$ and all of whose rows lie in $D_2$.

These definitions are shared by every statement of the mission.

**Formalization Note.** Tanner graphs are represented by their matrices `Matrix C V (ZMod 2)`. Minimum distances take values in `ℕ∞`, where the infimum of the empty set is `⊤`, which is the paper's $\infty$. The dimension $k_Q$ is the dimension of the quotient of $\mathcal C_X$ by $\mathcal C_Z^\perp\cap\mathcal C_X$, so no containment is presupposed. The dual code is `CodingTheory.dualCode` from the published definition `CodingTheory`. In $H_X$ and $H_Z$ the block $V_1\times V_2$ comes first (`Sum.inl`) and $C_1\times C_2$ second, as on p. 18; in the product code a column is indexed by a fixed second coordinate.
definition:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_CodingTheory

namespace TillichZemor.HGP

open Matrix
open scoped Kronecker

/-- The binary code of a Tanner graph with parity-check matrix `H` (rows = check nodes,
columns = variable nodes): the kernel of `H` (§2, p. 4). -/
def code {C V : Type*} [Fintype V] (H : Matrix C V (ZMod 2)) :
    Submodule (ZMod 2) (V → ZMod 2) :=
  LinearMap.ker H.mulVecLin

/-- Minimum distance of a binary linear code: the least Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword,
with the convention of p. 15 that it is `∞ = ⊤` for the zero code. -/
noncomputable def minDist {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ x ∈ D, ⨅ (_ : x ≠ 0), (hammingNorm x : ℕ∞)

/-- `d_X` of eq. (1), p. 4, for the CSS pair `(A, B) = (𝒞_X, 𝒞_Z)`: the least Hamming weight of a
vector of `A ∖ B^⊥` (`⊤` if there is none). `d_Z` is `cssDist B A`. -/
noncomputable def cssDist {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (A B : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ x ∈ A, ⨅ (_ : x ∉ CodingTheory.dualCode (ZMod 2) ι B), (hammingNorm x : ℕ∞)

/-- `k_Q` of eq. (2), p. 4: `dim (A / B^⊥)`, the quotient of `A` by `B^⊥ ∩ A`. -/
noncomputable def cssDim {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (A B : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (A ⧸ (CodingTheory.dualCode (ZMod 2) ι B).comap A.subtype)

section Product

variable {V₁ C₁ V₂ C₂ : Type*} [Fintype V₁] [Fintype C₁] [Fintype V₂] [Fintype C₂]
  [DecidableEq V₁] [DecidableEq C₁] [DecidableEq V₂] [DecidableEq C₂]

/-- The parity-check matrix `H_X = (H₁ ⊗ I_{n₂} | I_{r₁} ⊗ H₂ᵀ)` of `𝒞_X(𝒢₁ × 𝒢₂)`
(Definition 3, pp. 7–8; matrix form p. 18). Rows: checks `C₁ × V₂`; columns (qubits):
`(V₁ × V₂) ⊕ (C₁ × C₂)`. -/
def hx (H₁ : Matrix C₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) (H₂ : Matrix C₂ V₂ (ZMod 2)) :
    Matrix (C₁ × V₂) ((V₁ × V₂) ⊕ (C₁ × C₂)) (ZMod 2) :=
  Matrix.fromCols (H₁ ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix V₂ V₂ (ZMod 2))) ((1 : Matrix C₁ C₁ (ZMod 2)) ⊗ₖ H₂ᵀ)

/-- The parity-check matrix `H_Z = (I_{n₁} ⊗ H₂ | H₁ᵀ ⊗ I_{r₂})` of `𝒞_Z(𝒢₁ × 𝒢₂)`
(Definition 3, pp. 7–8; matrix form p. 18). Rows: checks `V₁ × C₂`. -/
def hz (H₁ : Matrix C₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) (H₂ : Matrix C₂ V₂ (ZMod 2)) :
    Matrix (V₁ × C₂) ((V₁ × V₂) ⊕ (C₁ × C₂)) (ZMod 2) :=
  Matrix.fromCols ((1 : Matrix V₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) ⊗ₖ H₂) (H₁ᵀ ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix C₂ C₂ (ZMod 2)))

/-- The quantum minimum distance `d_Q = min(d_X, d_Z)` of `𝒬(𝒢₁ × 𝒢₂)` (eq. (1)). -/
noncomputable def quantumDist (H₁ : Matrix C₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) (H₂ : Matrix C₂ V₂ (ZMod 2)) : ℕ∞ :=
  min (cssDist (code (hx H₁ H₂)) (code (hz H₁ H₂)))
    (cssDist (code (hz H₁ H₂)) (code (hx H₁ H₂)))

/-- The quantum dimension `k_Q = dim(𝒞_X / 𝒞_Z^⊥)` of `𝒬(𝒢₁ × 𝒢₂)` (eq. (2)). -/
noncomputable def quantumDim (H₁ : Matrix C₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) (H₂ : Matrix C₂ V₂ (ZMod 2)) : ℕ :=
  cssDim (code (hx H₁ H₂)) (code (hz H₁ H₂))

/-- The parity-check matrix of the hypergraph product `𝒢₁ ⊗ 𝒢₂` (Definition 7, p. 12):
variable nodes `V₁ × V₂`, check nodes `(C₁ × V₂) ⊕ (V₁ × C₂)`. -/
def tensorTanner (H₁ : Matrix C₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) (H₂ : Matrix C₂ V₂ (ZMod 2)) :
    Matrix ((C₁ × V₂) ⊕ (V₁ × C₂)) (V₁ × V₂) (ZMod 2) :=
  Matrix.fromRows (H₁ ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix V₂ V₂ (ZMod 2))) ((1 : Matrix V₁ V₁ (ZMod 2)) ⊗ₖ H₂)

end Product

/-- The product code `𝒞₁ ⊗ 𝒞₂` (Definition 8, p. 12): the words `x : ι₁ × ι₂ → 𝔽₂`, viewed as
`ι₁ × ι₂` matrices, whose columns `i ↦ x (i, j)` all lie in `D₁` and whose rows
`j ↦ x (i, j)` all lie in `D₂`. -/
def productCode {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} (D₁ : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι₁ → ZMod 2))
    (D₂ : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι₂ → ZMod 2)) : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι₁ × ι₂ → ZMod 2) :=
  (⨅ j : ι₂, D₁.comap (LinearMap.funLeft (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (fun i : ι₁ => (i, j)))) ⊓
  (⨅ i : ι₁, D₂.comap (LinearMap.funLeft (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (fun j : ι₂ => (i, j))))

end TillichZemor.HGP
source: Tillich and Zémor, Quantum LDPC codes with positive rate and minimum distance proportional to n^{1/2}, arXiv:0903.0566v2, p. 4 eqs (1)–(2) and Tanner graphs (i)–(ii), Definition 3 (pp. 7–8), Definitions 7–8 (p. 12), Definition 11 (p. 13), p. 15 (∞ convention), p. 18 (H_X, H_Z)
